body.text: Power washing done with the wood in mind

Power washing has a reputation for being aggressive, and used carelessly it can be. Restore My Deck treats it as a controlled process rather than a blast-and-go job. We adjust pressure based on wood species and condition, since pressure-treated pine, cedar and older weathered boards all respond differently to the same nozzle setting. The goal is to lift dirt, algae, grease and old stain off the surface without driving water into the grain or tearing up soft fibres, which is a real risk on decks built with pressure-treated pine, the most common decking material across Kitchener-Waterloo backyards.
Why pressure-treated pine needs extra care

Pressure-treated pine is manufactured to resist rot and insects, but that treatment process leaves the wood relatively soft compared to cedar or hardwood decking. Under too much pressure, a washer can leave visible striping, raise the grain unevenly or blow small chunks of fibre right off the board. Because so many decks in this region are built with pressure-treated pine, we default to a gentler setting and lean on our wood cleaners to do more of the work chemically rather than mechanically, which gets the same clean result without the risk of surface damage.

After washing, we apply a wood brightener, sometimes called a wood conditioner, to the deck. Cleaning solutions and hard water can leave wood slightly alkaline, which dulls its natural colour and can interfere with how evenly a stain absorbs afterward. A brightener neutralizes that pH, restores the wood's natural tone, and opens the grain slightly so whatever finish goes on next penetrates more evenly. This step is easy to skip and easy to notice when it has been skipped, since decks that go straight from washing to staining without a brightener often end up blotchy.

body.text: Power washing versus low-pressure deck cleaning

We offer both power washing and a lower-pressure cleaning option, and the right choice depends on your deck's condition and wood type. Heavier buildup, thicker algae, or a deck that has not been touched in several years usually calls for power washing's stronger mechanical action, paired with our wood-safe process to keep it controlled. A deck that was cleaned and stained more recently, or one built from particularly soft or aged wood, is often better served by the gentler approach covered on our /deck-cleaning page. If you are not sure which applies to your deck, tell us its age, wood type and how long it has been since its last cleaning and we will recommend the right service during your free quote.
We recommend power washing your deck at least once a year to keep dirt, algae and grime from building up between staining or sealing cycles.

A properly power washed and brightened deck absorbs stain or sealant far more evenly than one that has simply been rinsed off. This matters most heading into a Southwestern Ontario winter, when whatever finish is on the deck is the only thing standing between the wood and months of snow, ice and freeze-thaw cycling. If power washing reveals rot, soft boards or loose railings that were hidden under dirt and old stain, we will flag those issues right away so you can decide whether to move straight into repair and staining or handle the cosmetic work in stages.
Timing power washing around Ontario's seasons

Late spring through early fall gives the most consistent conditions for power washing in Southwestern Ontario, since the wood needs a stretch of dry, moderate weather to dry out fully afterward before any stain or sealant goes on. Washing right before winter can also be worthwhile on its own, since it clears away a season's worth of buildup and gives the deck a cleaner surface heading into months where it will not see much maintenance. We work around the forecast either way, avoiding days with rain in the immediate outlook so the cleaning products and brighteners have time to do their job properly.

faqs.q: Is power washing safe for pressure-treated pine?
faqs.a: Yes, when the pressure is calibrated correctly. We reduce pressure and rely more on wood cleaners for pine specifically, since it is softer than cedar and more prone to surface damage from excessive pressure.

faqs.q: What is a wood brightener and why is it used?
faqs.a: A wood brightener is a conditioning treatment applied after washing that restores the wood's natural pH balance and colour, helping any stain or sealant applied afterward absorb more evenly.

faqs.q: How is power washing different from your regular deck cleaning service?
faqs.a: Power washing uses stronger mechanical pressure alongside wood cleaners and brighteners, which suits decks with heavier buildup. Our lower-pressure cleaning service is gentler and better suited to more delicate or recently maintained wood.

faqs.q: How often should I power wash my deck?
faqs.a: We recommend power washing at least once a year to prevent dirt, algae and old finish from accumulating and to keep the deck ready for staining or sealing.

faqs.q: Will power washing remove old stain or paint?
faqs.a: It effectively removes loose, flaking or worn finish, though full removal depends on how many coats have built up over the years and the condition of the existing finish.

faqs.q: What does deck power washing typically cost?
faqs.a: Power washing and fence cleaning services typically run $800 to $1,200 by area, confirmed with a free, no-obligation quote based on your deck's size and condition.
